questions: Does "handle all water" mean every well must end up completely empty?
Can a single operation apply to only one well, or could it be shared across multiple wells at once?
Is the total operation count the sum of per-well operation counts, computed independently per row?
Is bucket capacity the same for every well?
What does "handle" mean precisely if not fully removing all water — could it include leaving some water below a threshold?
Is grid guaranteed to be rectangular?
What is returned for a well that already contains zero water?
answers: Yes, the goal is to fully empty every well of all its water.
No, one operation always applies to exactly one well — it lowers one bucket into one well only.
Yes, total operations = sum of ceil(well_units/capacity) computed independently per well/row.
Yes, already stated: capacity is the same for every well.
'Handle' means fully removing all water; there's no partial-removal threshold — it's the bucket-lowering count needed to empty each well completely.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume capacity is always positive.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume grid is rectangular.
Zero operations, since there's no water to remove.
